submission.justification: Algorithm-L2 gives the highest signal efficiency in the emulation: 92.2% at 35 GeV (100k events, allocated rate), versus 85.1% for L3 and 73.6% for L1. Changing the threshold to 30 GeV gave 91.9%, so efficiency is nearly flat in this range and 35 GeV is kept to match the 2025 reference point. The main open issue is the 4.0 us FPGA latency hard constraint. None of the project documents (candidate_specs.md, rate_allocation.md, simulation_summary_2025.md, links.md, schedule.md, meeting notes) and no tool gives the latency of any candidate, and the emulation returns efficiency only. I therefore could not verify that L2 meets 4.0 us, and I have not claimed it does. L2 is an iterative topological clustering algorithm, which is plausibly the most latency-expensive of the three, so this is a real risk. Before adoption, the FPGA latency of L2 must be measured. If it exceeds 4.0 us, the fallback is Algorithm-L3 at 35 GeV (85.1%) if its latency is verified, otherwise Algorithm-L1 (73.6%), which is the simplest fixed-window sum and most likely to be fast.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
FPGA latency must not exceed 4.0 us (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: No document or tool reports latency for any candidate. The simulation returns efficiency only. Latency for Algorithm-L2 must be measured on the FPGA before this recommendation is adopted.

requirements.requirement: Goal: highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated rate (8 kHz)
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L2 at 35 GeV gives 92.2% efficiency, the highest of the three candidates (L3 85.1%, L1 73.6%). The emulation reports efficiency at the allocated rate; the rate itself was not independently checked.
